55709-the-crimson-azaleas-a-novel.title: A Novel
55709-the-crimson-azaleas-a-novel.creator: H. De Vere Stacpoole
55709-the-crimson-azaleas-a-novel.description: A book by H. De Vere Stacpoole. ,  Along the road to Nikko  Either side the way,  Thundering great camellia trees  Decked with blossoms gay,  Adorn the road to Nikko,  The mountain road to Nikko,  In the month of May.”

arxiv-2009-09829.title: Generalized Leverage Score Sampling for Neural Networks Thanks: The authors would like to thank Michael Kapralov for suggestion of this topic.
arxiv-2009-09829.creator: Jason D. Lee, Ruoqi Shen, Zhao Song, Mengdi Wang, Zheng Yu
arxiv-2009-09829.description: Abstract Leverage score sampling is a powerful technique that originates from theoretical computer science, which can be used to speed up a large number of fundamental questions, e.g. linear regression, linear programming, semi-definite programming, cutting plane method, graph sparsification, maximum matching and max-flow.

arxiv-2106-08972.title: Redefining Neural Architecture Search of Heterogeneous Multi-Network Models by Characterizing Variation Operators and Model Components
arxiv-2106-08972.creator: Unai Garciarena, Roberto Santana and Alexander Mendiburu
arxiv-2106-08972.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Unai Garciarena, Roberto Santana and Alexander Mendiburu. With neural architecture search methods gaining ground on manually designed deep neural networks -even more rapidly as model sophistication escalates-, the research trend shifts towards arranging different and often increasingly complex neural architecture search spaces. In this conjuncture, delineating algorithms which can efficiently explore these search spaces can result in a significant improvement over currently used methods, which, in general, randomly select the structural variation operator, hoping for a performance gain.

arxiv-2108-04567.title: Robust and Dexterous Dual-arm Tele-Cooperation using Adaptable Impedance Control
arxiv-2108-04567.creator: Keyhan Kouhkiloui Babarahmati, Mohammadreza Kasaei, Carlo Tiseo, Michael Mistry, Sethu Vijayakumar
arxiv-2108-04567.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Keyhan Kouhkiloui Babarahmati, Mohammadreza Kasaei, Carlo Tiseo, Michael Mistry, Sethu Vijayakumar. In recent years, the need for robots to transition from isolated industrial tasks to shared environments, including human-robot collaboration and teleoperation, has become increasingly evident. Building on the foundation of Fractal Impedance Control (FIC) introduced in our previous work, this paper presents a novel extension to dual-arm tele-cooperation, leveraging the non-linear stiffness and passivity of FIC to adapt to diverse cooperative scenarios.

arxiv-2110-04919.title: Strong correlation, Bloch bundle topology, and spinless Haldane-Hubbard model
arxiv-2110-04919.creator: Ilya Ivantsov, Alvaro Ferraz, Evgenii Kochetov
arxiv-2110-04919.description: Abstract Different realizations of the Hubbard operators in different Hilbert spaces give rise to various microscopic lattice electron models driven by strong correlations. In terms of the Gutzwiller projected electron operators, the most familiar examples are the conventional t − J t-J model and the BCS-Hubbard model at strong coupling.

arxiv-2112-04643.title: Autoregressive Quantile Flows for Predictive Uncertainty Estimation
arxiv-2112-04643.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . Numerous applications of machine learning involve representing probability distributions over high-dimensional data. We propose autoregressive quantile flows, a flexible class of normalizing flow models trained using a novel objective based on proper scoring rules. Our objective does not require calculating computationally expensive determinants of Jacobians during training and supports new types of neural architectures, such as neural autoregressive flows from which it is easy to sample.

arxiv-2210-05601.title: Electrodynamics in geometric algebra Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2210-05601.creator: Sylvain D. Brechet
arxiv-2210-05601.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sylvain D. Brechet. We consider the electrodynamics of electric charges and currents in vacuum and then generalise our results to the description of a dielectric and magnetic material medium : first in spatial algebra (SA) and then in space-time algebra (STA).

arxiv-2306-11576.title: Deep Learning Methods for Retinal Blood Vessel Segmentation: Evaluation on Images with Retinopathy of Prematurity
arxiv-2306-11576.creator: 1 st Gorana Gojić, 2 nd Veljko Petrović, 3 rd Radovan Turović, 4 th Dinu Dragan, 5 th Ana Oros, 6 th Dušan Gajić, 7 th Nebojša Horvat
arxiv-2306-11576.description: Abstract Automatic blood vessel segmentation from retinal images plays an important role in the diagnosis of many systemic and eye diseases, including retinopathy of prematurity. Current state-of-the-art research in blood vessel segmentation from retinal images is based on convolutional neural networks.

arxiv-2409-02293.title: Size-dependent second-order-like phase transitions in Fe nanocluster melting from low-temperature structural isomerization
arxiv-2409-02293.creator: Louis E. S. Hoffenberg, Alexander Khrabry, Yuri Barsukov, Igor D. Kaganovich, David B. Graves
arxiv-2409-02293.description: Abstract In this work, the melting phase transitions of F ​ e n Fe_{n} nanoclusters with 10 ≤ n ≤ 100 10\leq n\leq 100 atoms are investigated using classical many-body molecular dynamics simulations. For many cluster sizes, surface melting occurs at much lower temperatures than core melting.

arxiv-2412-13167.title: Search for new interactions at the micron scale with a vector force sensor
arxiv-2412-13167.creator: Gautam Venugopalan, Clarke A. Hardy, Kenneth Kohn, Yuqi Zhu, Charles P. Blakemore, Alexander Fieguth, Jacqueline Huang, Chengjie Jia, Meimei Liu, Lorenzo Magrini, Nadav Priel, Zhengruilong Wang, Giorgio Gratta
arxiv-2412-13167.description: Abstract The search for new gravity-like interactions at the sub-millimeter scale is a compelling area of research, with important implications for the understanding of classical gravity and its connections with quantum physics. We report improved constraints on Yukawa-type interactions in the 10 ​ μ ​ m 10\,\mathrm{\mu m} regime using optically levitated dielectric microspheres as test masses.

arxiv-2501-06933.title: Neural Equilibria for Long-Term Prediction of Nonlinear Conservation Laws
arxiv-2501-06933.creator: Jose Antonio Lara Benitez, Kareem Hegazy, Junyi Guo, Ivan Dokmanić, Michael W. Mahoney, Maarten V. de Hoop
arxiv-2501-06933.description: Abstract Nonlinear conservation laws govern a broad class of important physical systems in science and industry and are central to scientific machine learning (SciML). Large general-purpose models offer speed, but replacing the numerical and physical structure of solvers often compromises stability, accuracy, and physical faithfulness.

arxiv-2509-13108.title: Variational data assimilation for the wave equation in heterogeneous media
arxiv-2509-13108.creator: Erik Burman, Janosch Preuss, Tim van Beeck
arxiv-2509-13108.description: Abstract In recent years, several numerical methods for solving the unique continuation problem for the wave equation in a homogeneous medium with given data on the lateral boundary of the space-time cylinder have been proposed. This problem enjoys Lipschitz stability if the geometric control condition is fulfilled, which allows devising optimally convergent numerical methods.

arxiv-2511-22392.title: Muddy Waters
arxiv-2511-22392.creator: Hans van Ditmarsch
arxiv-2511-22392.description: Abstract In the 2013 Advent calender of the Berlin Mathematics Research Center MATH+, Gerhard Woeginger presents a novel hat problem with an uncommon initial announcement. Although the information given is insufficient for the hat bearers to learn their colour, they are informed that the colours have been chosen so that they can learn their colour.

arxiv-2603-25508.title: What happens to wavepackets of fermions when scattered by the Maldacena-Ludwig wall?
arxiv-2603-25508.creator: Yuji Tachikawa, Keita Tsuji, Masataka Watanabe

arxiv-2604-24197.creator: Mr. Shuai Wu, Ms. Xue Li, Mrs. Yanna Feng, Prof. Yufang Li, Mr. Zhijun Wang, Mr. Ran Wang

pmc-10598968.title: SARS-CoV-2 spike protein S1 activates Cx43 hemichannels and disturbs intracellular Ca2+ dynamics
pmc-10598968.creator: Juan Prieto-Villalobos, Claudia M Lucero, Maximiliano Rovegno, Gonzalo I Gómez, Mauricio A Retamal, Juan A Orellana
pmc-10598968.description: BackgroundSevere acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) causes the ongoing coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). An aspect of high uncertainty is whether the SARS-CoV-2 per se or the systemic inflammation induced by viral infection directly affects cellular function and survival in different tissues.

pmc-10619067.title: Emotional intelligence, workplace conflict and job burn-out among critical care physicians: a mediation analysis with a cross-sectional study design in Egypt
pmc-10619067.creator: Zeinab A Kasemy, Asmaa Fady Sharif, Nadia M Bahgat, Shimaa Abdelsattar, Asmaa A Abdel Latif
pmc-10619067.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine the association between the effect of emotional intelligence on job burn-out and the mediating effect of workplace conflict management among critical care physicians.Design and settingA cross-sectional study design was deployed.ParticipantsThe studied sample comprised 144 critical care physicians working at two Egyptian tertiary care public hospitals.

pmc-10632882.title: Improving surgical safety checklist utilisation at 23 public health facilities in Ethiopia: a collaborative quality improvement project
pmc-10632882.creator: Dawit Yifru Bete, Manuel Kassaye Sibhatu, Melaku Gebremichael Godebo, Ilili Jemal Abdulahi, Tewodros Worku Liyew, Seye Mesfin Minas, Emily Bryce, Tigistu Adamu Ashengo, John Varallo
pmc-10632882.description: BackgroundIn 2009, the WHO introduced the surgical safety checklist (SSC) as one of the interventions for improving patient safety. The systematic use of structured checklists during surgery has been shown to reduce perioperative morbidity and mortality. However, SSC utilisation has been challenging in low-income and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia.

pmc-11342681.title: ΔNp63 bookmarks and creates an accessible epigenetic environment for TGFβ-induced cancer cell stemness and invasiveness
pmc-11342681.creator: Eleftheria Vasilaki, Yu Bai, Mohamad Moustafa Ali, Anders Sundqvist, Aristidis Moustakas, Carl-Henrik Heldin
pmc-11342681.description: Backgroundp63 is a transcription factor with intrinsic pioneer factor activity and pleiotropic functions. Transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) signaling via activation and cooperative action of canonical, SMAD, and non-canonical, MAP-kinase (MAPK) pathways, elicits both anti- and pro-tumorigenic properties, including cell stemness and invasiveness.

pmc-11535818.title: Electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy-guided preoperative lung nodule localization in video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS): a learning curve analysis
pmc-11535818.creator: Menghua Xue, Ke Lan, Xiaolong Yan, Tao Jiang, Xiaoping Wang, Feng Tian, Yunfeng Ni, Jinbo Zhao
pmc-11535818.description: BackgroundElectromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy (ENB) has been widely used to mark small peripheral pulmonary nodules (PPNs) in video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) resection. This technique offers the advantages of a high accuracy and fewer complications. However, few studies have analyzed the learning curve of ENB-guided preoperative localization. We aimed to describe the learning curve and factors influencing ENB-guided thoracoscopic pulmonary nodule resection.

pmc-11551904.title: Multimodal Temperature Readout Boosts the Performance of CuInS2/ZnS Quantum Dot Nanothermometers
pmc-11551904.creator: Magdalena Duda, Pushkar Joshi, Anna Borodziuk, Kamil Sobczak, Bozena Sikora-Dobrowolska, Sebastian Maćkowski, Allison M. Dennis, Łukasz Kłopotowski
pmc-11551904.description: Fluorescent nanothermometers are positioned to revolutionize research into cell functions and provide strategies for early diagnostics. Fluorescent nanostructures hold particular promise to fulfill this potential if nontoxic, stable varieties allowing for precise temperature measurement with high thermal sensitivities can be fabricated. In this work, we investigate the performance of micelle-encapsulated CuInS2/ZnS core/shell colloidal quantum dots (QDs) as fluorescent nanothermometers.

pmc-12529801.title: Continuous glucose monitoring in non-insulin-dependent type-2 diabetes – rationale for CGM-NIDDM study
pmc-12529801.creator: Carolin Rädel, Andreas Wienke, Rainer U Pliquett
pmc-12529801.description: Type-2 diabetes is treated by general practitioners and diabetologists in a stepwise manner with an emphasis on lifestyle modifications. Glucose monitoring is mandatory to gauge the effect of lifestyle modifications or medical therapies in order to identify the need for therapy escalation, if treatment goals are not met.

pmc-12563249.title: Essential Concepts in Artificial Intelligence: A Guide for Pediatric Providers
pmc-12563249.creator: Laura Elena Mendoza Bolivar, Michael Satzer, Jennifer M Lynch
pmc-12563249.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has exploded in public awareness over recent years and is already beginning to reshape the health care sector. Yet, even as AI becomes more prevalent, it remains a mystery to many providers who lack hands-on exposure during their training or on the job.

pmc-12632031.title: Improving succinic acid production by tuning polysulfides metabolism in Yarrowia lipolytica
pmc-12632031.creator: Xiaokun Zhang, Zhiyong Cui, Yongzhen Xia, Qingsheng Qi, Luying Xun, Huaiwei Liu, Qingda Wang
pmc-12632031.description: BackgroudSuccinic acid (SA) is a significant C4-dicarboxylic acid with broad applications in the food, chemical, and pharmaceutical industries. In microbial SA production, Yarrowia lipolytica shows great potential. Polysulfides are vital for maintaining redox balance and cellular health in yeast.ResultsIn this study, we changed the polysulfides metabolism of Y. lipolytica to enhance SA production.

pmc-12800528.title: From trauma surgery to acute care surgery: a 4-year observational study at a single trauma center in Korea
pmc-12800528.creator: Jung-Woo Woo, Jae Yool Jang, Yo Seok Cho, Hongkyung Shin, Chan Yong Park
pmc-12800528.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeThe acute care surgery (ACS) model establishes the capacity to immediately accommodate nontraumatic emergency surgery requiring urgent treatment while simultaneously elevating the existing trauma care system to the highest level. This study aims to evaluate the 4-year experience of operating after expanding the trauma surgery domain to ACS at this institution, which was designated as a lower-level trauma center by the local government in 2020.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted using clinical records for patients who underwent surgery in the Division of Trauma

pmc-13088868.title: Advanced Platelet‐Rich Fibrin in Surgical Management of Medication‐Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw: A Prospective Case Series Study
pmc-13088868.creator: Besim Hajdari, Lavdie Leci Morina, Granit Gashi, Gloriosa Dobra, Besir Salihu, Venera Bimbashi
pmc-13088868.description: BackgroundMedication‐related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a severe complication associated with antiresorptive or antiangiogenic therapy. Surgical debridement is the mainstay of treatment for moderate to advanced disease, while adjunctive regenerative approaches such as advanced platelet‐rich fibrin (A‐PRF) may enhance soft tissue healing.

pmc-13169857.title: Acute response and neurophysiological mechanisms of mindfulness meditation in emotional eating
pmc-13169857.creator: Roy Rongyue Zeng, Rangchun Hou, Hiu Yin Lai, Hei Yuen Huang, Ka Siu Lau, Ka Yan Hung, Rachel Kwok, Nestor Vinas Guasch, Daniel Kwasi Ahorsu, Tiev Miller, Yushen Dai, Pablo Cruz-Gonzalez, Yan Li, Benson Wui-Man Lau, Jack Jiaqi Zhang, Dalinda Isabel Sanchez Vidana
pmc-13169857.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionEmotional eating often leads to adverse health outcomes. Understanding how mindfulness influences emotional eating is crucial for developing strategies to promote healthier eating behaviors and well-being. This study aims to investigate the mechanism and acute response to a mindfulness meditation practice on emotional eating by examining immediate post-intervention effects on brain activity and neurophysiological differences between individuals with and without emotional eating.MethodsForty-nine adults were recruited and allocated into two groups based on the emotional eating subscale score of the Dutch Eating Behavior

pmc-13418887.title: Peroxydisulfate Activation by Lignosulfonate-Derived Iron–Carbon Catalyst for Tetracycline Hydrochloride Removal: Contributions of 1O2 and Iron Cycle
pmc-13418887.creator: Chun Xiao, Jinxi Chen, Yin Yang, Wu Ren, Lihong Ai, Yue Lu, Hongjun Li, Jiahui Zhang, Jiangfei Cao
pmc-13418887.description: A lignosulfonate-derived iron–carbon composite catalyst was fabricated via hydrothermal pyrolysis and employed to activate peroxydisulfate (PDS) for tetracycline hydrochloride (TCH) degradation. The optimized LFC possessed a porous carbon matrix uniformly decorated with Fe0/Fe3O4/Fe2O3 crystals, providing abundant active sites for catalytic reactions.
